label: thm:QOPd1=1
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:QOPd1=1}
The linear transformation $(x, \bm y) \in [-1,1] \rtimes \triangle^{d} \mapsto \bm u \in \triangle^{d+1}$ defined by
$$
  \bm u = \phi(x, \bm y) = \left(y_1, \ldots, y_{d-1}, \, \tfrac12(1-|\bm y|-x),  \tfrac12(1-|\bm y|+x) \right)
$$
is a bijection between $[-1,1]\rtimes \triangle^{d_2}$ and  $\triangle^{d+1}$. Moreover, under this linear transformation, 
the weight function $\bm W_{\mu,{\boldsymbol{\kappa}}}^{{\mathbb B}\rtimes \triangle}(x, \bm y)$ with ${\boldsymbol{\kappa}} = ({\kappa}_1,\ldots, {\kappa}_d)$ becomes
$$
    \bm W_{\bm {\beta}}^\triangle ({\bm u}) = 2^{2\mu-1} u_1^{{\kappa}_1} \cdots u_{d-1}^{{\kappa}_{d-1}} 
      (1-|\bm u|)^{{\kappa}_d} u_d^{\mu -\frac12} u_{d+1}^{\mu -\frac12}.
$$
In particular, let $\{\bm T_{\bm j, n}^{\bm {\beta}}: |\bm j|  = n, \, \bm j \in {\mathbb N}_0^{d+1}\}$ be an orthogonal basis
of ${\mathcal V}_n(\triangle^{d+1}, \bm W^\triangle_{\bm {\beta}})$ on the simplex $\triangle^{d+1}$; then
$$
   \bm Q_{\bm j, n}^{\mu, {\boldsymbol{\kappa}}} (x,\bm y) = \bm T_{\bm j, n}^{\bm {\beta}}\left(y_1, \ldots,  y_{d-1}, 
       \tfrac12(1-|\bm y|-x),  \tfrac12(1-|\bm y|+x) \right)
$$
for $|\bm j| = n$ consists of an orthogonal basis for 
${\mathcal V}_n\big([-1,1]\rtimes \triangle^d, \bm W_{\mu, {\boldsymbol{\kappa}}}^{{\mathbb B}\rtimes \triangle}\big)$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
The inverse of the linear transform ${\bm u} \mapsto (x, \bm y)$ is easily seen as given by 
$$
  x= u_{d+1}-u_d, \, y_1 = u_1, \ldots, y_{d-1} = u_{d-1}, \, y_d = 1-|\bm u|.
$$
It follows that $u_{d+1}-u_d = x$ and $u_d+u_{d+1} = 1 - |\bm y|$. In particular, $|x| \le 1-|\bm y|$ for 
$(x, \bm y) \in {\mathbb B}^{1} \! \rtimes \triangle^{d_2}$ 
becomes $|u_d- u_{d+1}| \le u_d+u_{d+1}$, which is equivalent to $u_d \ge 0$ and $u_{d+1} \ge 0$. Moreover, $1-|\bm u| = y_d$, 
so that $(x,\bm y)$ is mapped to $\bm u \in \triangle^{d+1}$. Moreover, the Jacobian $\partial (x, \bm y)/\partial \bm u = 2$, which
shows that the linear transformation is a bijection. Furthermore, 
$$
  \bm W_{\mu,\bm {\kappa}}^{[-1,1]\rtimes \triangle}(x, \bm y) = \prod_{i=1}^d y_i^{{\kappa}_i} (1-|\bm y|-x)^{\mu-\frac12} (1-|\bm y|+x)^{\mu-\frac12} 
     = \bm W_{\bm {\beta}}^\triangle ({\bm u})  
$$
with $\bm u \in \triangle^{d+1}$. Since the affine transformation preserves orthogonality, an orthogonal basis for 
${\mathcal V}_n\big({\mathbb B}^1 \rtimes \triangle^{d_2}, \bm W_{\mu,{\boldsymbol{\kappa}}}^{{\mathbb B}\rtimes \triangle}\big)$ can be derived from 
that of ${\mathcal V}_n(\triangle^{d+1}, \bm W^\triangle_{\bm {\beta}})$.

label: eq:Pn_d=1
title: Proposition
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
According to Theorem \ref{thm:QOPd1=1} and with $\bm {\beta}$ in \eqref{eq:beta}, we have the relation
$$
  \bm P_n^{1,d}\left(\bm W_{\mu, {\boldsymbol{\kappa}}}^{[-1,1] \times \triangle}; (\bm x,\bm y), (\bm u, \bm v)\right) 
  = \bm P_n \left(\bm W_{\beta}^\triangle; \phi(\bm x,\bm y), \phi(\bm u, \bm v)\right).
$$ 
Hence, the closed-form formula for $\bm P_n\left(\bm W_{\mu, {\boldsymbol{\kappa}}}\right)$ can be deduced from the addition
formula \eqref{eq:add-simplex} on the simplex $\triangle^{d+1}$. In particular, 
\begin{align*}
  \xi_\triangle\left(\phi(x,\bm y), \phi(u, \bm v), \bm t \right) & = \sum_{i=1}^{d-1} \sqrt{y_i v_i} \, t_i + 
    \tfrac12 \sqrt{ 1-|\bm y | - x} \sqrt{ 1-|\bm v | - u} \, t_d \\
 & +   \tfrac12 \sqrt{ 1-|\bm y | + x} \sqrt{ 1-|\bm v | + u} \, t_{d+1} +
     \sqrt{y_d v_d} \,t_{d+2},
\end{align*}
where we have used $1- |\phi(x, \bm y)| = y_d$. In the statement of the theorem, we have shuffled the order of
$t_d, t_{d+1}, t_{d+2}$ of the above expression in the definition of $\eta(x, \bm y, u, \bm v, \bm t)$.

label: prop:Pd=IntPd=1
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:Pd=IntPd=1}
For $\mu \ge 0$ and ${\boldsymbol{\kappa}} =({\kappa}_1,\ldots, {\kappa}_d)$ with ${\kappa}_i \ge -\frac12$, 
\begin{align} \label{eq:P=IntP}
  & \bm P_n^{d_1,d_2} \big(\bm W_{\mu, {\boldsymbol{\kappa}}}^{{\mathbb B}\rtimes \triangle}; (\bm x,\bm y), (\bm u, \bm v)\big)  \\
   = &\, c_{\mu-\frac12} \int_{-1}^1 
     \bm P_n^{1,d_2}\left(\bm W_{\mu+\frac{d_1 -1}{2}, {\boldsymbol{\kappa}}}^{[-1,1]\rtimes \triangle}; \big(\zeta (\bm x,\bm y,  \bm u,\bm v; s),\bm y\big), \big(1-|\bm v|, \bm v\big) \right) 
  (1-s^2)^{\mu-1} \mathrm{d} s, \notag 
\end{align} 
where  
$$
\zeta (\bm x,\bm y,  \bm u,\bm v; s) = \frac{{\langle} \bm x, \bm u {\rangle} + s \sqrt{(1-|\bm y|)^2 -\|\bm x\|^2}  \sqrt{(1-|\bm v|)^2 -\|\bm u\|^2}}{1-|\bm v|},
$$
and $|\zeta (\bm x,\bm y,  \bm u,\bm v; s)|\le 1$ for $(\bm x, \bm y), (\bm u, \bm v) \in {\mathbb B}^{d_1} \!\rtimes \triangle^{d_2}$ 
and $s \in [-1,1]$. Moreover,  the identity holds in the limit \eqref{eq:limitInt} if $\mu = 0$.
head: environment

label: eq:P=IntP2
title: Proof
body_md:
In terms of the orthogonal polynomials \eqref{eq:Qbasis} and their norms \eqref{eq:Q_OPNorm}, and the definition of 
the reproducing kernel on the unit ball, 
\begin{align*}                      
\bm P_n^{d_1,d_2} \left(\bm W_{\mu, {\boldsymbol{\kappa}}}^{{\mathbb B}\rtimes \triangle}; (\bm x,\bm y), (\bm u, \bm v)\right) & = \sum_{m=0}^n \frac{(|{\boldsymbol{\kappa}}|+ 2\mu+ d_1 + d_2)_{2m}}{(2\mu+d_1)_{2m}} \frac1{\bm h_{\bm k,m}^{\mu,{\mathbb B}}  
       \bm h_{\bm j,m}^{({\boldsymbol{\kappa}}, {\alpha}+2m),\triangle}} \\
 & \times  \sum_{\bm j = n-m} \bm T_{\bm j, n-m}^{({\boldsymbol{\kappa}}, 2m +2\mu+d_1-1)}(\bm y) 
      \bm T_{\bm j, n-m}^{({\boldsymbol{\kappa}}, 2m+2\mu+d_1-1)}(\bm v) \\
 & \times  (1-|\bm y|)^m (1-|\bm v|)^m \bm P_m\left(W_\mu^{\mathbb B}; \frac{\bm x}{1-|\bm y|}, \frac{\bm u}{1-|\bm v|} \right). \notag 
\end{align*}
Hence, by the addition formula \eqref{eq:add-ball}, we obtain
\begin{align}\label{eq:P=IntP2}
& \bm P_n^{d_1,d_2}  \left(\bm W_{\mu, {\boldsymbol{\kappa}}}^{{\mathbb B}\rtimes \triangle}; (\bm x,\bm y), (\bm u, \bm v)\right)
  = \sum_{m=0}^n \frac{(|{\boldsymbol{\kappa}}|+ 2\mu+ d_1 + d_2)_{2m}}{(2\mu+d_1)_{2m}} \frac{1}{ \bm h_{\bm j,m}^{({\boldsymbol{\kappa}}, {\alpha}+2m),\triangle}} \\
 &\qquad \times  \sum_{\bm j = n-m} \bm T_{\bm j, n-m}^{({\boldsymbol{\kappa}}, 2m +2\mu+d_1-1)}(\bm y) 
      \bm T_{\bm j, n-m}^{({\boldsymbol{\kappa}}, 2m+2\mu+d_1-1)}(\bm v) \notag \\
 & \qquad \times  (1-|\bm y|)^m (1-|\bm v|)^m c_\mu \int_{-1}^1 Z_m^{\mu+\frac{d_1-1}{2}}
     \left(\frac{\zeta (\bm x,\bm y, \bm u,\bm v; s)}{1-|\bm y|} \right)
  (1-s^2)^{\mu-1} \mathrm{d} s. \notag 
\end{align}
Now, using \eqref{eq:Qbasis_d1=1} and \eqref{eq:Q_OPNorm_d1=1}, we obtain for the case $d_1=1$ and ${\alpha} = 2\mu + d_1-1=2\mu$,
\begin{align}\label{eq:reprodPd=1}
& \bm P_n^{1,d_2}\big(\bm W_{\mu, {\boldsymbol{\kappa}}}^{{\mathbb B}\rtimes \triangle}; (x,\bm y), (1-|\bm v|, \bm v)\big) 
= \sum_{m=0}^n \frac{(|{\boldsymbol{\kappa}}|+ 2\mu+ d_2 +1)_{2m}}{(2\mu+1)_{2m}}  \frac{1}{ \bm h_{\bm j,m}^{({\boldsymbol{\kappa}}, 2\mu+2m),\triangle}} \\
& \times  \sum_{\bm j = n-m} \bm T_{\bm j, n-m}^{({\boldsymbol{\kappa}}, 2\mu+2m)}(\bm y)  \bm T_{\bm j, n-m}^{({\boldsymbol{\kappa}}, 2\mu+2m)}(\bm v) 
  (1-|\bm y|)^m (1-|\bm v|)^m Z_m^\mu \left(\frac{x}{1-|\bm y|}\right), \notag 
\end{align}
where we have used the relation 
$$
    \frac{1}{\sqrt{h_m^\mu}} C_m^\mu(1) C_m^\mu (t) = Z_m^\mu(t). 
$$
Setting $\mu \to \mu + \frac{d_1-1}{2}$ and $x = \zeta (\bm x,\bm y, \bm u,\bm v; s)$ in \eqref{eq:reprodPd=1}, 
and comparing its right-hand side with the right-hand side of \eqref{eq:P=IntP2} shows that \eqref{eq:P=IntP} holds.

label: eq:convolu
title: Definition
body_md:
For $\mu \ge 0$ and ${\kappa}_i \ge -\frac12$, let $ {\alpha} = |{\boldsymbol{\kappa}}| + 2\mu + d_1+d_2-1$. For 
$f\in L^1\big({\mathbb B}^{d_1} \!\rtimes \triangle^{d_2}, \bm W_{\mu,{\boldsymbol{\kappa}}}^{{\mathbb B}\rtimes \triangle}\big)$ 
and $g \in L^1([-1, 1], w_{{\alpha}, -\frac12})$, define the pseudo convolution of $f$ and $g$ by
\begin{equation} \label{eq:convolu}
 f\ast g (\bm x,\bm y) = \int_{{\mathbb B}^{d_1} \!\rtimes \triangle^{d_2}} f(\bm u,\bm v) T^{\mu,{\boldsymbol{\kappa}}} g\big ( (\bm x,\bm y), (\bm u,\bm v) \big)
    \bm W_{\mu, {\boldsymbol{\kappa}}}^{{\mathbb B}\rtimes \triangle} (\bm u, \bm v) \mathrm{d} \bm u \mathrm{d} \bm v
\end{equation}
where the operator $g \mapsto T^{\mu,{\boldsymbol{\kappa}}} g$ is defined by 
\begin{align*}
T^{\mu,{\boldsymbol{\kappa}}} g \big ( (\bm x,\bm y), (\bm u,\bm v) \big)
 =  & \, \bm b_{\mu,{\boldsymbol{\kappa}}} \int_{[-1,1]^{d+1}} \int_{-1}^1 g \big( 2 \xi(\bm x, \bm y, \bm u, \bm v; \bm s, \bm t)^2-1 \big) \notag \\
   &\times \prod_{i=1}^{d_2-1} (1-t_i^2)^{{\kappa}_i-\frac12} (1-|\bm t|^2)^{{\kappa}_{d_2}-\frac12}  \prod_{i=1}^2 (1-s_i^2)^{\mu - 1}  \mathrm{d} \bm t\, \mathrm{d} \bm s,
\end{align*}
in which $\xi(\bm x, \bm y, \bm u, \bm v; \bm s, \bm t)$ is defined as in the addition formula \eqref{eq:addition}.

title: Proof
body_md:
By \eqref{eq:QbasisV0} and \eqref{eq:Q_V0Norm} with ${\gamma} = -1$ so that ${\alpha} = d_1-2$, and using the addition formula 
for the spherical harmonics, the reproducing kernel satisfies,  
\begin{align*}
  {\mathsf P}_n  \big({\mathsf W}_{-1, {\boldsymbol{\kappa}}}^{{\mathbb S}\rtimes \triangle},  (\bm x, \bm y), & (\bm u, \bm v) \big) 
  =  \sum_{m=0}^n \sum_{|\bm j| = n-m} \sum_\ell \frac{(|{\boldsymbol{\kappa}}| + d_1+d_2-1)_{2m}}{(d_1-1)_{2m}}\frac{1}{\bm h_{\bm j,m}^{({\boldsymbol{\kappa}}, {\alpha}+ 2m), \triangle}}\\
     & \times \bm T_{\bm j, n-m}^{({\boldsymbol{\kappa}}, \alpha+2m)}(\bm y) \bm T_{\bm j, n-m}^{({\boldsymbol{\kappa}}, \alpha+2m)}(\bm v) (1-|\bm y|)^m (1-|\bm v|)^m 
       Z_m^{\frac{d_1-2}{2}}({\langle} \xi,\eta {\rangle}),
\end{align*}
where $\bm x  = (1-|\bm y|) \xi$ and  $\bm u  = (1-|\bm v|) \eta$. Comparing with \eqref{eq:reprodPd=1} with $\mu = \frac{d_1-2}{2}$, 
we obtain 
$$
{\mathsf P}_n  \big({\mathsf W}_{-1, {\boldsymbol{\kappa}}}^{{\mathbb S}\rtimes \triangle},  (\bm x, \bm y), (\bm u, \bm v) \big) 
 = \bm P_n^{1,d_2}\left(\bm W_{\frac{d_1-2}{2}, {\boldsymbol{\kappa}}}^{{\mathbb S}\rtimes \triangle}; 
      \big((1-|\bm y|) {\langle} \xi,\eta{\rangle},\bm y\big), (1-|\bm v|, \bm v)\right).  
$$
As a consequence, the integral identity follows from that of \eqref{eq:Pn_d=1} and its integrand becomes 
\begin{align*}
&  \xi_0(\bm x, \bm y, \bm u, \bm v; s, \bm t) = \eta\big( (1-|\bm y|) {\langle} \xi,\eta{\rangle},\bm y, 1-|\bm v|, \bm v); (\bm t,s) \big)  \\ \qquad  & 
 = \sqrt{y_1 v_1} \, t_1 + \cdots + \sqrt{y_d v_d} \, t_d + \frac12 \sqrt{(1-|\bm y|)(1+{\langle} \xi,\eta{\rangle})} \sqrt{2 (1-|\bm v|)}\, s, 
\end{align*}
which simplifies to the stated formula for $\xi_0(\bm x, \bm y, \bm u, \bm v;  s, \bm t)$ and completes the proof.

title: Proposition
body_md:
Let $d_1 \ge 2$. For $(\bm x, \bm y), (\bm u,\bm v) \in {\mathbb S}^{d_1-1}\!\rtimes \triangle^{d_2}$, define 
$$ 
  {\mathsf d}_{{\mathbb S}\rtimes \triangle}\big((\bm x, \bm y), (\bm u,\bm v) \big) = \arccos \left[ \sqrt{y_1 v_1} + \cdots + \sqrt{y_d v_d} 
     + \sqrt{\frac{{\langle} \bm x,\bm u{\rangle} +  (1-|\bm y|)(1- |\bm v|)}{2}} \right].
$$ 
Then ${\mathsf d}_{{\mathbb S}\rtimes \triangle}(\cdot,\cdot)$ defines a distance function on ${\mathbb S}^{d_1-1}\!\rtimes \triangle^{d_2}$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
By its definition, ${\mathsf d}_{{\mathbb S}\rtimes \triangle} (\cdot,\cdot)$ is symmetric in its variables. 
Since $\|\bm x\| = 1-|\bm y|$ and $\|\bm u\| = 1-|\bm v|$, we obtain
$$
0 \le \sqrt{y_1 v_1} + \cdots + \sqrt{y_d v_d} + \sqrt{\frac{{\langle} \bm x,\bm u{\rangle} +
   (1-|\bm y|)(1-|\bm v|)}{2}}  \le 1
$$
by the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality, so that ${\mathsf d}_{{\mathbb S}\rtimes \triangle} \big((\bm x, \bm y), (\bm u,\bm v) \big) \ge 0$ for all 
$\big((\bm x, \bm y), (\bm u,\bm v) \big) \in {\mathbb S}^{d_1-1}\!\rtimes \triangle^{d_2}$. Furthermore, 
${\mathsf d}_{{\mathbb S}\rtimes \triangle} \big((\bm x, \bm y), (\bm x,\bm y) \big) =
\arccos 1 = 0$. Thus, it remains to verify that ${\mathsf d}_{{\mathbb S}\rtimes \triangle} (\cdot,\cdot)$ satisfies the triangle inequality. 
Let $F: {\mathbb S}^{d_1-1}\!\rtimes \triangle^{d_2} \mapsto {\mathbb R}^{d_1 + d_2+1}$ be defined by
$$
  F(\bm x, \bm y) = \left(\frac{\bm x}{ \sqrt{2(1-|\bm y|)}}, \frac{\sqrt{1-|\bm y|}}{\sqrt{2}}, \sqrt{y_1}, \cdots, \sqrt{y_{d_2}}\right).
$$
Using $\|\bm x\| = 1- |\bm y|$, it is easy to see that $\|F(\bm x, \bm y)\|^2 = 1$, so that $F(\bm x, \bm y) \in {\mathbb S}^{d_1+d_2}$. 
Moreover, for $(\bm x, \bm y), (\bm u, \bm v) \in {\mathbb S}^{d_1-1}\!\rtimes \triangle^{d_2}$, 
setting $\bm x = (1-|\bm y|) \xi$ and $\bm u = (1-|\bm v|) \eta$, then
\begin{align*}
   {\langle} F(\bm x, \bm y),  F(\bm u, \bm v) {\rangle} 
       & =\frac{{\langle} \bm x, \bm u{\rangle} }{2 \sqrt{1-|\bm y|}\sqrt{1- |\bm v|}} + \frac{\sqrt{1-|\bm y|}\sqrt{1- |\bm v|}}{2}+ \sqrt{y_1 v_1}+ \cdots+
         \sqrt{y_d v_d} \\
      & =   \frac{\sqrt{1-|\bm y|}\sqrt{1- |\bm v|} (1+{\langle} \xi, \eta{\rangle})}{2} + \sqrt{y_1 v_1}+ \cdots+ \sqrt{y_d v_d} \\
      & =  \sqrt{ \frac{{\langle} \bm x, \bm y {\rangle}+ (1-|\bm y|) (1- |\bm v|)}{2}}   + \sqrt{y_1 v_1}+ \cdots+ \sqrt{y_d v_d}.
\end{align*}
In particular, this implies immediately that 
$$
  {\mathsf d}_{{\mathbb S}\rtimes \triangle}\big((\bm x, \bm y), (\bm u,\bm v) \big) = {\mathsf d}_{{\mathbb S}} \big ( F(\bm x, \bm y), F(\bm u, \bm v)\big),
$$
where ${\mathsf d}_{\mathbb S}$ is the distance function of ${\mathbb S}^{d_1+d_2}$. As a consequence, the triangle inequality 
of ${\mathsf d}_{{\mathbb S}\rtimes \triangle}$ follows from that of ${\mathsf d}_{\mathbb S}$. This completes the proof.
head: environment

title: Proposition
body_md:
Let $d_1, d_2 \ge 1$. For $(\bm x, \bm y), (\bm u,\bm v) \in {\mathbb B}^{d_1}\!\rtimes \triangle^{d_2}$, define 
\begin{align*}
 & {\mathsf d}_{{\mathbb B}\rtimes \triangle}\big((\bm x, \bm y), (\bm u,\bm v) \big)  =   \arccos \Big( \sqrt{y_1 v_1} + \cdots + \sqrt{y_d v_d}  \\
     & \qquad
     +   \sqrt{\frac12 \left( {\langle} \bm x,\bm u{\rangle} + (1-|\bm y|)(1- |\bm v|))+ \sqrt{(1-|\bm y|)^2- \|\bm x\|^2} \sqrt{(1-|\bm v|)^2- \|\bm u\|^2}\right)}\,  \Bigg ). 
\end{align*} 
Then ${\mathsf d}_{{\mathbb B}\rtimes \triangle}(\cdot,\cdot)$ defines a distance on ${\mathbb B}^{d_1}\!\rtimes \triangle^{d_2}$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Taking a cue from the relation between the distance functions for ${\mathbb B}^d$ and ${\mathbb S}^d$, for $(\bm x, \bm y)$
and $(\bm u, \bm v)$ in ${\mathbb B}^{d_1}\!\rtimes \triangle^{d_2}$, we introduce the notation
$$
  \bm X =  \left(\bm x, \sqrt{(1-|\bm y|)^2-\|\bm x\|^2}\right), \qquad  \bm U =  \left(\bm u, \sqrt{(1-|\bm v|)^2-\|\bm u\|^2}\right)
$$
and observe that $(\bm X, \bm y), (\bm U, \bm v) \in {\mathbb S}^{d_1}\!\rtimes \triangle^{d_2}$. Our definition then shows
$$
  {\mathsf d}_{{\mathbb B}\rtimes \triangle}\big((\bm x, \bm y), (\bm u,\bm v) \big) = {\mathsf d}_{{\mathbb S}^{d_1}\!\rtimes \triangle^{d_2}} \big((\bm X, \bm y), (\bm U, \bm v)\big), 
$$
where we have used ${\mathsf d}_{{\mathbb S}\!\rtimes \triangle} = {\mathsf d}_{{\mathbb S}^{d_1}\!\rtimes \triangle^{d_2}}$ to indicate the dependence on 
dimensions. From this identity follows readily that ${\mathsf d}_{{\mathbb B}\rtimes \triangle}$ is indeed an appropriate distance on 
${\mathbb B}^{d_1}\!\rtimes \triangle^{d_2}$.

label: thm:Q_BSig_d1=1
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:Q_BSig_d1=1}
The mapping $(x, \bm y) \in [-1,1] \rtimes {\mathbb R}_\Sigma^{d} \mapsto \bm u \in {\mathbb R}_+^{d+1}$ defined by
$$
  \bm u = \phi(x, \bm y) = \left(y_1, \ldots, y_{d-1}, \, \tfrac12(|\bm y|-x),  \tfrac12(|\bm y|+x) \right)
$$
is a bijection between ${\mathcal V}_n\big([-1,1]\rtimes {\mathbb R}_\Sigma^{d_2}, \bm W_{\mu,{\boldsymbol{\kappa}}}^{{\mathbb B}\rtimes \Sigma}\big)$ 
and  ${\mathbb R}_+^{d+1}$. Moreover, under this linear transformation, the weight function 
$\bm W_{\mu,{\boldsymbol{\kappa}}}^{{\mathbb B}\rtimes \Sigma}(x, \bm y)$ with ${\boldsymbol{\kappa}} = ({\kappa}_1,\ldots, {\kappa}_d)$ becomes
$$
    \bm W_{\bm {\beta}}^L ({\bm u}) = 2^{2\mu-1} u_1^{{\kappa}_1} \cdots u_{d-1}^{{\kappa}_{d-1}} {\bm u}_d^{\mu-\frac12} u_{d+1}^{\mu -\frac12}
      \mathrm{e}^{-|{\bm u}|},
$$
where ${\bm \beta} = ({\kappa}_1,\ldots, {\kappa}_{d-1}, \mu-\frac12,\mu-\frac12) \in {\mathbb R}^{d+1}$. In particular, let $\{\bm L_{\bm j, n}^{\bm {\beta}}: 
|\bm j|  = n, \, \bm j \in {\mathbb N}_0^{d+1}\}$ be an orthogonal basis of ${\mathcal V}_n({\mathbb R}_+^{d+1}, \bm W^L_{\bm {\beta}})$ on 
the ${\mathbb R}_+^{d+1}$. Then 
\begin{equation} \label{eq:OP_B-Sig_d1=1}
   \bm Q_{\bm j, n}^{\mu, {\boldsymbol{\kappa}}} (x,\bm y) = \bm L_{\bm j, n}^{\bm {\beta}}\left(y_1, \ldots,  y_{d-1}, 
       \tfrac12(|\bm y|-x),  \tfrac12(|\bm y|+x) \right)
\end{equation}
for $|\bm j| = n$ consist of an orthogonal basis for ${\mathcal V}_n\big([-1,1]\rtimes {\mathbb R}_\Sigma^d, \bm W_{\mu, {\boldsymbol{\kappa}}}^{[-1,1] \rtimes \Sigma}\big)$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
The inverse of the linear transform ${\bm u} \mapsto (x, \bm y)$ is easily seen as given by 
$$
  x= u_{d+1}-u_d, \, y_1 = u_1, \ldots, y_{d-1} = u_{d-1}, \, y_d = |\bm u| - 2 (u_1+ \cdots + u_{d-1}). 
$$
It follows that $u_d+u_{d+1} = |\bm y|$, so that $|x| \le |\bm y|$ for $(x, \bm y) \in [-1,1]\rtimes {\mathbb R}_\Sigma^d$ 
becomes $|u_d- u_{d+1}| \le u_d+u_{d+1}$, which is equivalent to $u_d \ge 0$ and $u_{d+1} \ge 0$, so ${\bm u} \in {\mathbb R}_+^{d+1}$. 
Furthermore, $|{\bm u}| = |{\bm y}| + |{\bm y}'|$, so that 
$$
  \bm W_{\mu,\bm {\kappa}}^{[-1,1]\rtimes \Sigma}(x, \bm y) = \prod_{i=1}^d y_i^{{\kappa}_i} (|\bm y|-x)^{\mu-\frac12} 
      (|\bm y|+x)^{\mu-\frac12} \mathrm{e}^{-|{\bm y}|- |yb'|} = 2^{2\mu-1} \bm W_{\bm {\beta}}^L ({\bm u})  
$$
with $\bm u \in {\mathbb R}_+^{d+1}$. Thus, an orthogonal basis for ${\mathcal V}_n\big([-1,1]\rtimes {\mathbb R}_\Sigma^{d_2}, 
\bm W_{\mu,{\boldsymbol{\kappa}}}^{{\mathbb B}\rtimes \Sigma}\big)$ can be derived from that of ${\mathcal V}_n({\mathbb R}_+^{d+1}, \bm W^L_{\bm {\beta}})$.

label: prop:Pd=IntPd_BSig
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:Pd=IntPd_BSig}
For $\mu > 0$ and ${\boldsymbol{\kappa}} =({\kappa}_1,\ldots, {\kappa}_d)$ with ${\kappa}_i > -\frac12$, 
\begin{align} \label{eq:P=IntPBSig}
  & \bm P_n^{d_1,d_2} \big(\bm W_{\mu, {\boldsymbol{\kappa}}}^{{\mathbb B}\rtimes \Sigma}; (\bm x,\bm y), (\bm u, \bm v)\big)  \\
   = &\, c_{\mu-\frac12} \int_{-1}^1 
     \bm P_n^{1,d_2}\left(\bm W_{\mu+\frac{d_1 -1}{2}, {\boldsymbol{\kappa}}}^{[-1,1]\rtimes \Sigma}; 
         \big(\zeta (\bm x,\bm y,  \bm u,\bm v; s),\bm y\big), \big(|\bm v|, \bm v\big) \right) 
  (1-s^2)^{\mu-1} \mathrm{d} s, \notag 
\end{align} 
where  
$$
\zeta (\bm x,\bm y,  \bm u,\bm v; s) = \frac{{\langle} \bm x, \bm u {\rangle} + s \sqrt{|\bm y|^2 -\|\bm x\|^2}\sqrt{|\bm v|^2 -\|\bm u\|^2}}{|\bm v|},
$$
and $|\zeta (\bm x,\bm y,  \bm u,\bm v; s)|\le 1$ for $(\bm x, \bm y), (\bm u, \bm v) \in {\mathbb B}^{d_1}\! \rtimes {\mathbb R}_\Sigma^{d_2}$ 
and $s \in [-1,1]$.
head: environment

title: Theorem
body_md:
Let ${\boldsymbol{\kappa}} =({\kappa}_1,\ldots, {\kappa}_d)$, ${\kappa}_i > - 1/2$ and $\mu > 0$. Then, for $({\bm x}, \bm y)$ and $({\bm u}, \bm v)$ in 
${\mathbb B}^{d_1} \rtimes {\mathbb R}_\Sigma^{d_2}$,
\begin{align*} 
 & \bm P_n^{d_1,d_2} \left(\bm W_{\mu, {\boldsymbol{\kappa}}}^{{\mathbb B}\rtimes \Sigma}; (x,\bm y), (u, \bm v)\right) 
  = {\bm c}_{\mu,{\boldsymbol{\kappa}}} \int_{[0,\pi]^{d_2}} L_n^{|{\boldsymbol{\kappa}}| + 2\mu +d_1+d_2-1} \big(\xi({\bm x}, {\bm y}, {\bm u}, \bm v; s, \bm {\theta}) \big) \\
  & \quad \times \prod_{i=1}^{d_2-1} j_{{\kappa}_i-\frac12}\big ( \sqrt{y_i v_i} \sin {\theta}_i\big) 
   j_{\mu-\frac12} \Bigg(\sqrt{\tfrac{{\langle} {\bm x},{\bm u}{\rangle}+|{\bm y}|\cdot |{\bm v}| + s \sqrt{|{\bm y}|^2-\|{\bm x}\|^2}\sqrt{|{\bm v}|^2-\|{\bm u}\|^2} }{2} }   \sin {\theta}_d \Bigg) \\
 &\quad \times \exp \left( -\sum_{i=1}^{d-1} \sqrt{y_i v_i} \cos {\theta}_i- \sqrt{\tfrac{{\langle} {\bm x},{\bm u}{\rangle}+|{\bm y}|\cdot |{\bm v}| 
   + s \sqrt{|{\bm y}|^2-\|{\bm x}\|^2}\sqrt{|{\bm v}|^2-\|{\bm u}\|^2} }{2} } \cos {\theta}_{d}\right)\\
  & \quad \times \prod_{i=1}^{d-1} (\sin {\theta}_i)^{2 {\kappa}_i} (\sin {\theta}_d)^{2\mu-1} (1-s^2)^{\mu-1} \mathrm{d} \bm{{\theta}} \mathrm{d} s,
\end{align*}
where ${\bm c}_{\mu,{\boldsymbol{\kappa}}} =  c_{\mu-\frac12} {\bm c}_{{\boldsymbol{\kappa}}, \mu-\frac12}^L$, and
\begin{align*}                      
 \xi(x, \bm y, u, \bm v; \bm t)  = & |{\bm y}'| + |{\bm y}| +|{\bm v}'| + |{\bm v}| + 2 \sum_{i=1}^{d-1} \sqrt{y_i v_i} \cos {\theta}_i \\
   & + 2 \big({\langle} {\bm x},{\bm u}{\rangle}+|{\bm y}|\cdot |{\bm v}| + s \sqrt{|{\bm y}|^2-\|{\bm x}\|^2}\sqrt{|{\bm v}|^2-\|{\bm u}\|^2} \big) \cos {\theta}_d.  \notag
\end{align*}

label: prop:OP_SS-SIg
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:OP_SS-SIg}
For ${\boldsymbol{\kappa}} \in {\mathbb R}^{d_2}$ with ${\kappa}_i > -1$, $1 \le i \le d_2-1$, and ${\kappa}_{d_2} > - d_1$. Let ${\alpha} = {\kappa}_{d_2} + d_1 -1$. Define  
\begin{equation*}                     
 {\mathsf Q}_{\bm j, \ell, m}^n(\bm x,\bm y) = \hat {\bm L}_{\bm j, n-m}^{({\boldsymbol{\kappa}}, \alpha+2m)}(\bm y) |\bm y|^m 
      {\mathsf Y}_{\ell}^m \left(\frac{\bm x}{|\bm y|}\right). 
\end{equation*}
Then $\{{\mathsf Q}_{\bm j, \ell, m}^n: |\bm j| = n-m, \, 1 \le \ell \le \dim {\mathcal H}_m^{d_1}, \, 0 \le m  \le n, \bm j \in {\mathbb N}_0^{d_2}\}$ 
is an orthogonal basis of ${\mathcal V}_n({\mathbb S}^{d_1-1}\!\rtimes {\mathbb R}_\Sigma^{d_2}, {\mathsf W}_{{\boldsymbol{\kappa}}}^{{\mathbb S}\rtimes \Sigma})$. Moreover, 
the squared norm of ${\mathsf Q}_{\bm j, \ell, m}^n$ 
is given by 
\begin{equation*}                     
   {\mathsf h}_{m,n}^{{\boldsymbol{\kappa}}}                                                                        
       =   \frac{\bm b^L_{({\boldsymbol{\kappa}}',\alpha)}}{\bm b^L_{({\boldsymbol{\kappa}}', \alpha + 2m)}} \bm h_{\bm j,m}^{({\boldsymbol{\kappa}}', {\alpha}+ 2m), L}
       =  ({\alpha}+1)_{2m}\bm h_{\bm j,m}^{({\boldsymbol{\kappa}}', {\alpha}+ 2m), L}.  
\end{equation*}

label: thm:additionS-Sig
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:additionS-Sig}
Let $d_1 \ge 2$ and ${\kappa}_1,\ldots, k_{d_2-1} \ge -\frac12$ and ${\kappa}_{d_2} = -1$. Then 
\begin{align*}                      
 & {\mathsf P}_n  \big({\mathsf W}_{{\boldsymbol{\kappa}}}^{{\mathbb S}\rtimes \Sigma},  (\bm x, \bm y), (\bm u, \bm v) \big) 
    =  {\mathsf c}_{{\boldsymbol{\kappa}}} \int_{[0,\pi]^{d_2}} L_{2n}^{|{\boldsymbol{\kappa}}| + d_1+d_2-2}
    \big( \xi_0(\bm x, \bm y, \bm u, \bm v; \bm {\theta})\big) \notag \\
  & \times \prod_{i=1}^{d_2-1} j_{{\kappa}_i-\frac12}\big ( \sqrt{y_i v_i} \sin {\theta}_i\big)
     j_{\frac{d_1-3}{2}}  \Big(\sqrt{\tfrac{ {\langle} {\bm x},{\bm u}{\rangle} +|{\bm y}|\cdot|{\bm v}|}2} \sin {\theta}_{d_2} \Big) \\
  &\times \exp \left( -\sum_{i=1}^{d_2-1} \sqrt{y_i v_i} \cos {\theta}_i-  \frac12 \sqrt{{\langle} {\bm x}, {\bm u}{\rangle} + |{\bm y}|\cdot |{\bm v}|}\cos {\theta}_{d_2} \right)
   \prod_{i=1}^{d_2-1} (\sin {\theta}_i)^{2{\kappa}_i} (\sin {\theta}_{d_2})^{d_1-3} \mathrm{d} \bm{{\theta}},
\end{align*}
where ${\bm c}_{\boldsymbol{\kappa}} =  {\bm c}_{{\boldsymbol{\kappa}}', \frac{d_1-3}{2}, \frac{d_1-3}{2}}^L$, and
\begin{align*}                       
 \xi_0({\bm x}, \bm y, {\bm u}, \bm v; \bm \theta)  = & |{\bm y}'| + |{\bm y}| +|{\bm v}'| + |{\bm v}| + 2 \sum_{i=1}^{d-1} \sqrt{y_i v_i} \cos {\theta}_i
  +  \sqrt{({\langle} {\bm x},{\bm u}{\rangle} + |{\bm y}|\cdot |{\bm v}|} \cos {\theta}_{d_2}  . \notag
\end{align*}
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
The proof is similar to that of Theorem \ref{thm:additionV0}. From the explicit formulas for the orthogonal basis and the
norms in Proposition \ref{prop:OP_SS-SIg}, and applying the addition formula for the spherical harmonics, it follows 
that 
$$
{\mathsf P}_n  \big({\mathsf W}_{{\boldsymbol{\kappa}}}^{{\mathbb S}\rtimes \Sigma},  (\bm x, \bm y), (\bm u, \bm v) \big) 
 = \bm P_n^{1,d_2}\left(\bm W_{(\frac{d_1-2}{2},{\boldsymbol{\kappa}}')}^{[-1,1] \rtimes \Sigma} \big(|\bm y| {\langle} \xi,\eta{\rangle},\bm y\big), (|\bm v|, \bm v)\right).  
$$
Consequently, the addition formula for ${\mathsf W}_{{\boldsymbol{\kappa}}}^{{\mathbb S}\rtimes \Sigma}$ follows from Proposition \ref{prop:Pn_BSig_d1=1}.
